column1: # duration.tsv — the ONE golden table for the two formatDuration renderers
# (§20 erratum 268). internal/web/format.go renders the duration an owner reads
# in the library and on the watch page; internal/notify/reply.go renders the
# duration the Discord bot's follow-up carries, and the two are byte-identical
# on purpose: "arc · 0:32" in a channel and "arc · 0:32" in the library are
# meant to be the same fact, and a divergence between them would be silent.
# The copy exists because the two packages do not import each other — DESIGN §3's
# import graph has no edge from the outbound-call package to the HTML renderer —
# which is exactly the situation nit sweep S11 found in humanBytes, where three
# copies had been left unpinned and one had drifted. So: one table, two tests
# (internal/web's TestFormatDuration and internal/notify's), and a change to
# either copy must match this file or edit it.
# The rounding rule this pins: seconds are rounded to NEAREST (the +500 before
# the divide), not floored, so a 5,999 ms clip reads 0:06 rather than 0:05 —
# and the hour branch appears only past an hour, so a short clip never carries
